title: World map with lines of latitude and longitude
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y5 lesson 7 (World map with latitude and longitude lines (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 7. Lines of latitude run east to west; lines of longitude run north to south. Use them to describe locations.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Is Iceland north or south of the Equator?
questions.model: Look at the letter: N. N means north. Iceland is north of the Equator.

questions.q: Is Sri Lanka east or west of Greenwich?
What is the latitude of the Equator?
Core: Find and label these on a world map: 54°N 2°W, 65°N 18°W, 19°S 47°E, 8°N 81°E.
questions.a: Great Britain, Iceland, Madagascar, Sri Lanka
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 54°N is well north; 2°W is just west of Greenwich: that is Great Britain.

questions.q: Extend: Which island is closest to the Equator: Sri Lanka, Sicily or Iceland?
Stretch: Bahrain is at about 26°N, 50°E. Describe where it is.
questions.a: North of the Equator and east of Greenwich, in the Persian Gulf, near Saudi Arabia

questions.q: Big question: how can you find any island on Earth with just two numbers?
questions.a: Latitude says how far north or south, longitude how far east or west; together they pinpoint it
